Executive structural synthesis

Poland's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as constructive but mixed. Growth Quality: Broad-based growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. Household Demand: Defensive / non-durable-led mix. External Sector: Export-supported external contribution. Across the five modules, 3 are favourable, 1 mixed/neutral and 1 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 17.7% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 48.2% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 52.0%. Total real GFCF growth was +7.5% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Strong real GFCF growth.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as productivity gains with labour-cost pressure. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew +2.7% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +4.0% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Elevated NULC growth; Large productivity gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as defensive / non-durable-led mix. Real household consumption grew +2.2% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 8.1% of nominal household expenditure and services for 37.6% in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Durable-goods demand contracting.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as export-supported external contribution. Net exports contributed +0.37 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Exports contributed +5.21 pp and imports -4.84 pp. Real exports grew +10.4% YoY while real imports grew +10.3% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
